text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.4% today as oil prices climbed on fresh Middle East supply concerns. Escalating tensions in Iran and Saudi Arabia—including reported attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and Iranian threats toward U.S. assets—have spooked energy markets and pushed crude prices higher, with world oil now trading at $125 per barrel. The stock has gained 12% over two weeks as these geopolitical risks have compounded.

The tightness extends beyond crude itself. The International Energy Agency warned that diesel supply will remain constrained well into 2027 due to Iran-related disruptions, falling inventories, and persistent demand—a supply squeeze that benefits refiners and integrated oil producers like ConocoPhillips, which have exposure to both crude and refined products.
